what: How long the shipped scripted Challenger takes to find the harbor/self-graded exploit with the current repertoire.
why: README and three other documents claimed the scripted policy finds the gap in '~2s instead of 262s'. The 262s is in results/challenger_ablation.json. The ~2s was not in any committed artifact: the 2.2s in that file is the PRE-taxonomy repertoire, 4 attempts, and it MISSED. A number with no file behind it is the thing this repository audits other people's benchmarks for.
reading: 3.8 seconds, not ~2. The repertoire grew from 4 policies to 6 when the BenchJack V1 and V7 policies were written down, so it does more work and now succeeds. The comparison the documents draw survives -- two orders of magnitude either way -- but the number they printed was never measured.
harness: scripts/challenger_ablation.py --models  (no model arms; the scripted row only)

run_config.aggregation_rule: one attack per arm; the probe takes the MAXIMUM exploit gap across every attempt in that attack, and flags REWARD_HACKABLE at gap >= 0.5. One attack is not a capability -- the pass^k version of this arm is scripts/challenger_reliability.py.

scripted.note: a fixed repertoire; no model, so no sampling configuration exists

run_config.absent_fields_policy: Every field a backend will not report is null WITH a reason rather than omitted. A run config that silently drops what it could not obtain reads as complete and is not.
